title: Two-variable AM-GM over the constructed rationals, proved by a producer-found sum-of-squares certificate
statement: For rationals x, y: x*y + x*y <= x*x + y*y. Equivalently 2xy <= x^2 + y^2, the two-variable AM-GM inequality, whose difference is the perfect square (x - y)^2.

formal.statement: theorem Rat.two_mul_le_sq_add_sq : ((x0 : Rat) -> ((x1 : Rat) -> Rat.le (Rat.add (Rat.mul x0 x1) (Rat.mul x0 x1)) (Rat.add (Rat.mul x0 x0) (Rat.mul x1 x1))))

evidence.supports: Rat.two_mul_le_sq_add_sq is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement, from a proof term the psatz PRODUCER searched for.
checkers: crate::psatz::rat::prove (the producer that emitted the term)
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example rat_theorem_inventory -- two_mul_le_sq_add_sq 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^theorem[[:space:]]Rat\.two_mul_le_sq_add_sq[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: The proof term was NOT written by a person. `crate::psatz::rat::prove` parsed the goal into a polynomial, factored the difference's Gram matrix over the affine basis with an exact rational LDL^T, cleared denominators to one integer scale, emitted the `sq_nonneg`/`add_nonneg` fold, proved the certificate's identity with `ring::rat::prove_eq`, and handed the assembled term to `Kernel::add_declaration`. `rat_prelude/psatz_inequalities.rs` has NO hand-written fallback: if the producer declines, `build_rat_prelude` fails, so the presence of this theorem in the environment is itself the evidence that the search ran and succeeded. `Kernel::add_declaration` re-checks the emitted term against the stated type, so a line in this tool's output for the exact name is a machine-checked proof having been admitted. `--release` is used for speed, not necessity: this binary builds logic/nat/int/rat and no constructed prelude. `grep -c` (never `-q`) both avoids a SIGPIPE-under-pipefail false negative and independently asserts the whitespace-anchored `theorem` row is present, so a theorem demoted to an axiom would fail this check rather than pass it. A named filter matching nothing exits 1 in the tool itself, verified 2026-09-05 (`no_such_rat_theorem_xyz` -> exit 1), so a deleted theorem cannot read as a re-derived one. The separators are `[[:space:]]`, not `\t`: POSIX ERE does not interpret `\t` as a tab, so a tab-anchored pattern matches NOTHING under the GNU grep a script gets, while an interactive shell's ugrep wrapper masks it.

evidence.notes: `rat_theorem_inventory`'s third column is `Kernel::axiom_footprint` joined by commas, so an EMPTY third column is an empty footprint; `grep -cx ''` (never `grep -q`, which lies under `pipefail`) counts the blank field and exits 1 when there is none, so a theorem that grew a footprint fails rather than reporting a smaller number. Independently, `rat_prelude_tests::every_rat_declaration_is_checked_and_axiom_free` derives its population from `Environment::iter`, not from a literal list, and asserts an empty footprint for every `Rat.`-prefixed theorem or definition; measured 2026-09-05 the whole prelude is 454 derived, 454 with an empty footprint, 0 asserted.

evidence.supports: The producer that emitted this proof has a mutation control suite in which every registered mutant is killed, so the guards behind the certificate are load-bearing.
evidence.notes: Six mutants, RUN twice -- before and after these theorems joined the prelude -- all six killed both times, exit 0 both times, baseline 29 tests. The two the brief named: flipping a cleared form's coefficient sign killed 5 then 12, and changing the verified-witness refusal reason killed exactly 1 both times. The two counts that MOVED are the mutants that now also break `build_rat_prelude`, which is what the no-fallback design predicts. This row pins the PRODUCER's guards, not the statement: it says the search cannot silently degrade, and says nothing about the statement being true, which the kernel-term row above is what settles.

provenance.source: Statement written in `rat_prelude/psatz_inequalities.rs`; PROOF TERM searched for by the psatz producer (ADR-1649) and never written by hand. Canonical type copied verbatim from `target/release/examples/rat_theorem_inventory two_mul_le_sq_add_sq`, one name per invocation, release build. depends_on is the direct-edge set from `target/release/examples/theorem_dependency_inventory Rat.two_mul_le_sq_add_sq`, one name per invocation, restricted to edges that are themselves registered ledger facts -- every edge was, so nothing was dropped.

notes: Certificate: a single square `(x - y)^2` at scale 1, so no division step is emitted -- visible in the measured dependency edges, which include neither `Rat.le_or_lt` nor `Rat.lt_irrefl` (the `divide_by_scale` lemma set) nor `Rat.add_nonneg` (the fold never joins two summands, because there is only one square). depends_on is the direct-edge set from `theorem_dependency_inventory Rat.two_mul_le_sq_add_sq`, every entry of which is itself a registered ledger fact, so nothing was dropped in the mapping.
